manifest.claim_text: The magnetically induced E-field solver reproduces the closed-form (Sarvas / Heller-van Hulsteyn) solution for a spherically symmetric conductor, validated independently of any neural-response model.
manifest.falsified_by: relative error above tolerance against the closed form, or a mesh-refinement study that does not converge at the advertised order
manifest.consequence_if_failed: The induced-field solver may not be used for TMS E-field prediction, target engagement or pose ranking; every downstream induction-dependent claim is suspended (N3 does not cover this: it validates conduction, not induction).
non_goals: These checks establish code correctness only. Numerical correctness is necessary, never sufficient: agreement with recorded signals is stronger, held-out perturbation stronger still (thesis §0.2).

subchecks.name: induced_efield
subchecks.description: Relative error against a closed-form solution, with no neural model in the loop.
subchecks.falsified_by: relative error above tolerance against the analytic solution

subchecks.name: reference_provenance
subchecks.description: Does the closed-form reference come from the same module as the solver?

metrics.name: induced_efield.reference_shares_module_with_solver
metrics.note: solver=scwbd.intervene.tms.efield, reference=scwbd.intervene.spectral_reference; shared provenance is not disqualifying, but it is a weaker test than an independent implementation and must not be described as independent validation

subchecks.name: reference_validity_domain
subchecks.description: The multipole/series reference converges like ratio**degree. Its a-priori error bound at this geometry must sit well below the solver error being measured, or the gate is measuring the reference.
subchecks.falsified_by: the reference is no more accurate than the solver it measures

metrics.name: reference.convergence_ratio
metrics.note: a/R_c at the validated geometry; the series converges like ratio**degree, so a ratio approaching 1 is not fixable by raising the degree

metrics.name: reference.bound_over_measured_error
metrics.note: a-priori reference bound 4.22e-06 / measured solver error 0.00215; the reference must be the more accurate of the two by a clear margin

notes: Induction, not conduction: this gate is what N3 does NOT cover.

STANDOFF ONLY. The reference series converges like (a/R_c)**degree. At a contact geometry (a/R_c ~ 0.955 for a coil element 4 mm off an 85 mm scalp) no feasible degree brings its bound below the solver error, so this gate validates the discretisation against a STANDOFF equivalent dipole, not against a contact coil. tms-robotics positions a coil in contact; that regime is gate N8_induced_efield_contact and it has not run.
The validity domain is a metric in this report, not a footnote: a reader who checks only the headline error still sees reference.convergence_ratio.

reference_validity_domain.does_not_cover: contact geometry. A coil element in contact with the scalp has a/R_c ~ 0.955, where no feasible degree brings the series bound below the solver error. This gate validates a STANDOFF equivalent dipole; the contact regime is gate N8_induced_efield_contact and has not run.

known_uninformative_fields.git_dirty_whole_tree: a whole-tree dirty flag always reads dirty during a run, because the run writes tracked output (reports/training/*.log, *.jsonl). It cannot distinguish modified source from a run writing its own log, so it is not recorded here and must not be gated on. Use source_dirty_paths.
